# New-ZbxLldFilterCondition

## SYNOPSIS

Builds a discovery filter condition for the -Filter conditions of New-ZbxDiscoveryRule and Set-ZbxDiscoveryRule.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxLldFilterCondition [-Macro] <string> [[-Value] <string>] [-FormulaId <string>] [-Operator <ZabbixConditionOperator>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A condition matches a low-level discovery macro against a regular expression, so only the discovered entities that pass become items, triggers and graphs. The New-ZbxLldFilterCondition cmdlet writes it as a hashtable keyed by the API's field names, which the -Filter conditions of New-ZbxDiscoveryRule and Set-ZbxDiscoveryRule take as it is, alone or in an array. -Macro and -Value are positional. Nothing is sent to the server, so the command needs no connection.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Build a condition that keeps the usual file systems

```powershell
New-ZbxLldFilterCondition FSTYPE '^(ext4|xfs|btrfs)$'
```

-Macro and -Value are positional: the LLD macro, written with or without {# }, and the regular expression it must match.

### Example 2: Filter what a discovery rule creates

```powershell
$conditions = @(
    New-ZbxLldFilterCondition FSTYPE '^(ext4|xfs|btrfs)$'
    New-ZbxLldFilterCondition FSNAME '^/(snap|run)/' -Operator NotRegexp
)
Get-ZbxHost -Name 'web-01' |
    New-ZbxDiscoveryRule -Name 'Mounted filesystems' -Key 'vfs.fs.discovery' -Type ZabbixActive -Delay '1h' -Filter @{ evaltype = 'And'; conditions = $conditions } |
    Select-Object Name, Key
```

The rule creates items only for the file systems whose {#FSTYPE} matches and whose {#FSNAME} does not.
